For 387-393 the page names only Yongshi (385), the title Prince of Yuanchuan ('in 387, they became a vassal to Former Qin after Guoren accepted their title of Prince of Yuanchuan') and Jincheng (388). The correction keeps the part of the shape within 150 km of Lanzhou (130 of the 516 cells, about 33,000 km2; only 33 cells lie within 80 km), so that the 394 gain (/ledger/2) draws the other 386 cells. notes: Cliopatria rows: Western Qin 387..438 has seven shapes. (1) The state runs 385-431 on the pages; Cliopatria starts two years late and ends seven years late (426 shape to 438, Northern Wei from 439). (2) From 414 Cliopatria adds a belt of about 94,000 km2 round Wuwei, Baiyin and Wuzhong that is the Later Liang's 400 shape and Later Qin's 410 shape and never the Northern Liang's; the Northern Liang page has Guzang (Wuwei) surrender in 411 and become the capital in 412, and Cliopatria's Northern Liang shape lies wholly west of Wuwei. This needs a decision by the reviewer: the Western Qin and the Northern Liang dossiers both correct it, the Later Qin dossier gives Wuwei away in 412 (confidence 1). (3) 400-408: the page has the state suspended and Qiangui a Later Qin general keeping his territory; Cliopatria gives the land to Later Qin from 402 and shows Western Qin until 401. (4) 426: repaired 2026-10-19. The Qifu Chipan page gives the 426 defeat as Xia's raid (Nan'an and Xiping taken, Fuhan attacked, then withdrawal), recorded as a contest with xia; no page has the Tuyuhun in 426, and the Huangshui land goes to the Tuyuhun in 430 (/ledger/15). (5) Xicheng still has no location on any page opened (Cliopatria-centroid placeholder); Tanjiao is Linxia Hui Autonomous Prefecture and Nan'an Dingxi on the Qifu Chipan page (Linxia and Longxi stand in). (6) Vassalages, not ledger events (the suzerain's dossier owns them): Former Qin 387 (Prince of Yuanchuan), Later Liang 395 briefly, Later Qin 400-409 and King of Henan 410, Jin 417 (Duke of Henan), Northern Wei offered 430. (7) The infobox gives no area, so the factor-of-two check could not be made. (8) The Western Qin page names no commanderies; all regions are discs or Cliopatria shapes. Page budget: six pages opened, all cited (the Qifu Chipan page at the reviewer's direction). Gazetteer: Longxi, Xining, Linxia and Lanzhou are places; Dingxi and Baiyin (glosses on the Qifu Chipan page) are not in the gazetteer and appear in text only. Repair of 2026-10-19: (9) the 387 shape was drawn from 387 and grew the map sixfold with no event; the 385-393 land is now the part of Cliopatria's Longxi shape within 150 km of Lanzhou, and the 394 gain draws the rest. (10) The Cliopatria cells dropped in 426 (134, of which 131 in its Tuyuhun shape) are the misplaced Southern Liang polygon at Linxia-Lintao, not the Huangshui valley at Xining; the Tuyuhun dossier's 430 gain is that polygon plus a north-west strip, a part of the land lost here in 430. (11) Yuanchuan: the Qifu Chipan page glosses it as Baiyin, the coordinates stay at Yuzhong (the Yuan River valley), unresolved.
